A short, personal list of resources I find useful, for students and anyone interested in my research areas.

## Bayesian Statistics

- [Bayesian Data Analysis](http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/book/) — Gelman et al.; the standard graduate reference, with a free PDF of the third edition.
- [Statistical Rethinking](https://xcelab.net/rm/) — Richard McElreath; an accessible introduction with recorded lectures.
- [Stan](https://mc-stan.org) — a probabilistic programming language for Bayesian modeling, with interfaces for R and Python.

## Functional Data Analysis

- [fda](https://cran.r-project.org/package=fda) — R package accompanying Ramsay and Silverman's *Functional Data Analysis*.
- [refund](https://cran.r-project.org/package=refund) — R package for regression with functional data.

## Neuroimaging Data and Tools

- [Human Connectome Project](https://www.humanconnectome.org) — large open dataset of brain imaging, including resting-state fMRI.
- [OpenNeuro](https://openneuro.org) — free repository of open neuroimaging datasets (MRI, EEG, MEG).
- [MNE-Python](https://mne.tools) — Python toolkit for processing and analyzing EEG and MEG data.
